body.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
body.justification: This is the constructive half of the honest-length frontier for arbitrary cell masses under fixed overlap and the explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, reports bootstrap and Gaussian intervals but warns that they need not attain nominal coverage when \(n\) and \(d\) are comparable. ArmstrongKolesar2021, Abstract and Sections 2--4, gives finite-sample bias-aware ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions and normal errors with known variance, whereas this theorem permits arbitrary categorical cell masses and only the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Painsky2022 treats individual unseen multinomial masses rather than an overlap-adjusted causal aggregate with marked outcomes.
body.consumer: A uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the saturated 401(k) application of ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024.
